sam: Quick sync — we need a canonical benchmark/harness that lets us compare kernel selection + batching heuristics across replay and synthetic traffic and ensure our metrics are apples-to-apples.

liam: +1. can we list the mandatory axes? sequence_len distribution, inter-arrival timings, kv-cache state (cold/warm), model quantization, kernel flags? :thinking_face: 

tanvi: add 'prefix cache hit rate' explicitly. replay harness can skew if we don't match client-side prefix reuse.

sam: Right. Proposed minimal test matrix:
- Traffic modality: synthetic (poisson+bursty) vs replayed traces
- KV cache: cold start, steady-state warm, 50% prefix-hit mix
- Sequence length buckets: short <32, mid 32-256, long >256 (weight per production distro)
- Kernel candidates: default, fast-matmul, quant-kernelex
- Batching params: continuous batching on/off, max_batch_size, max_latency_ms
- Model variant: fp16, int8-quant (same weights)

liam: For metrics, let's lock definitions now:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): wall clock from request recv to first token emit (include preemption/retries)
- TPOT (time-per-output-token): median per-token latency starting from t1
- p95/p99: reported on request-level tails for TTFT and full response latency
- QPS vs goodput: QPS = requests/sec. goodput = output_tokens/sec excluding failed/retried requests.

tanvi: Important: when we compute per-request latencies, use request completion semantics (i.e., full response emitted) and also include a 'partial-response' metric to catch streaming regressions.

ops-qa: bench-bot: ran synthetic run earlier and flagged a p95 TTFT increase ~7% after kernel switch. Details incoming.

bench-bot: test_id=1951234500
config:
```
harness: replay
trace: prod-sample-2025-11
kv_cache_policy: warm
batching: continuous:true,max_batch:64,max_delay_ms:8
kernel_candidates: [default,fast-matmul]
metrics: [TTFT,TPOT,p95,p99,QPS,goodput]
```
results summary: p95 TTFT 7% higher on fast-matmul vs default for short sequences (<32). QPS steady. Goodput down 3%.

sam: @liam any hypothesis?

liam: My guess: dispatch overhead for small sequences + heavier per-request kernel setup. fast-matmul wins on long sequences but has fixed dispatch cost. continuous batching masks some of that but with very short sequences we didn't fill batches.

tanvi: Could also be KV cache warmup interplay. fast-matmul handles KV layout differently (additional copy) — more costly when prefix hits are high.

sam: Actionable plan:
1) Run microbench: single-shot short sequences across kernels w/ isolated threads to measure kernel dispatch cost.
2) Replay with controlled prefix-hit ratios (0%, 50%, 100%).
3) Synthetic poisson experiments to stress batching under realistic inter-arrival jitter.
4) Collect TTFT/TPOT p50/p95/p99 + goodput, and produce delta vs baseline with bootstrap CI.

liam: I'll own (1) and (3). ops-qa will run (2) and (4).

ops-qa: timeline: run (2) today, (4) tomorrow. will post CI plots and raw csv.

tanvi: Reminder: make sure kernel selection uses same compilation flags and that quantized kernels use same dequant pathway. Otherwise not apples-to-apples.

sam: Also log per-request kernel decision tag so we can slice latencies by kernel at query time.

liam: I'll add a small agent in the harness that writes `kernel_choice` and `batch_size_at_dispatch` in the request metadata.

ops-qa: ack. I'll update the bench PR with the test matrix and expected output fields.

sam: Perfect. thanks everyone. let's re-sync after microbench results. :thumbsup:
